title: רב חנן בר אמי

paragraphs: Rav Chanan bar Ammi said: R. Pedat said: R. Yochanan said—Berakhot 55b. This is Ein Yaakov's reading, but the Gemara reads “Rav Huna bar Ammi said: R. Pedat said: R. Yochanan said.” Apparently it is a scribal error, since he is not mentioned elsewhere in the Talmud. Avodah Zarah 38a; Asheri has Rav Chana bar Ammi, etc. Immediately there, in the Gemara, after the matter in which Rav Chanan bar Ammi said: R. Pedat said: R. Yochanan said, it says, “The text itself: Rabbah bar bar Chana said: R. Yochanan said.” This appears a scribal error and should read “The text itself: Chanan said: R. Pedat said: R. Yochanan said.” Rif's bar Avdimi is a scribal error. Pesachim 101a, near the end: “R. Chanin bar Abaye said: R. Pedat said: R. Yochanan said” is certainly a scribal error and should read bar Ammi. In Ulpana's name; see there. R. Chiyya bar Ammi also spoke in Ulpana's name. I am uncertain whether one of the places is erroneous and they are all one person. “Shmuel said”—Berakhot; Gittin 52b; Shabbat 13a. Bar Rami is a scribal error, since immediately there it has bar Ammi; also end of Shemonah Sheratzim. Bekhorot 25a.
